correctness.rationale: For n≥3, all symmetric nonnegative row-stochastic matrices on C_n∘K_1 admit convex dihedral symmetrization without increasing SLEM. Exact two-by-two Fourier blocks show a lower bound from the first positive mode; strict decrease in backbone weight and strict convex minimization in leaf weight yield unique invariant optimizer. Explicit algebra gives a strictly positive gap protecting all negative Fourier eigenmodes for 0<u²≤3/2 and proves the bound attained for every n. Endpoint b=0 is excluded and all allowed boundaries handled. Closed-form 1/3-weight heuristic SLEM follows from mode bounds, then asymptotic gap ratio is 3/2. Standalone verify.py passed exact symbolic identities and dense spectra for all n=3..50, without confusing finite computations with proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full texts of the foundational 2004 FMMC paper and the 2007 symmetry paper were directly inspected, including the nearest cycle, wheel and cyclic perturbation families; an accessible broad general-bounds paper was also inspected. Actual source/alias searches and overlap comparisons did not reveal an exact all-n optimum on the cycle-with-private-leaves graph, nor an implication from a dominating exact statement. A prior complete-core corona formula differs in graph and spectral structure. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not an independence certificate.
residual_risks: Search index coverage and undiscovered literature on pendant-ring Markov chains may contain a result with equivalent formulas.

value.rationale: A cycle with one private pendant state per vertex is a standard sparse ring-with-leaves design; optimizing its uniform-stationary stochastic edge conductances is a natural global FMMC problem. The theorem gives a fully explicit all-size optimum with a nontrivial all-modes global certificate and a uniquely optimal symmetric architecture. Its 50% asymptotic spectral-gap improvement over two standard feasible heuristics quantifies a meaningful performance tradeoff due to pendant bottlenecks; it is not a mere finite-slice computation or special case of the earlier complete-core graph formula.
